teaching_notes.why_this_case_matters: KEEP example: the instruction forms one coherent local route objective (Turn around and go down the entranceway, heading toward the staircase. Turn to your left and…). The apparent action clauses do not establish a separate completed target with a useful, source-supported handoff.
teaching_notes.reusable_rule: Keep the instruction as one stage when its turns, traversal and target selection form one coupled maneuver and no independent intermediate completion point is stated. Preserve all action order and conditions in the same stage.
teaching_notes.five_element_focus: Check entry, target, complete ordered process, supported ending, and scoped conditions in the actual English text. Audit fields cannot replace missing words.
teaching_notes.handoff_focus: A boundary is not a physical stop. Verify the previous exit and next entry refer to the same established region/object/frame.
teaching_notes.retrieval_rule: Retrieve for short or tightly coupled routes where splitting at a turn, pass-by cue or descriptive observation would create an orientation-only stage without an independent navigation target.
teaching_notes.anti_pattern: Do not infer a new stage from sentence boundaries, multiple turns, or a landmark pass. Do not generalize this KEEP decision to routes that contain completed independent objectives.
teaching_notes.decision_reason: Several turns and pass-by actions form one continuous approach to a specified doorway position. No earlier action establishes a useful independent endpoint before the final stop.
teaching_notes.transfer_rule: Keep a continuous maneuver together when intermediate actions only establish orientation or route continuation and no independent completed objective supports a handoff.
